Risk Premia Analysis Dashboard

Six commodity buckets (Metals, Petroleum, Gas and Emissions, NGL, Precious, Agriculture), five sleeves each (Momentum, Carry, Carry-Momentum, Value, Skewness), combined by Equal Weight and Inverse Vol only. Log-return methodology, 5 bps costs, reporting from 2012-01-01 in three periods (P1 2012-2016, P2 2017-2021, P3 2022 onwards) plus a 2026 year-to-date column. All price data through 2026-10-29.
How to use this dashboard
  • Tabs across the top: one per bucket, plus By Style, Cross-Pair, Correlations and Notes (methods and data).
  • Blue filter bars mark every control you can change: period, commodity, metric.
  • Tables show IR for every period; click a period heading (or use the filter) to see that period's return, volatility and maximum drawdown.
  • Charts: tick or untick strategies above the chart, change the start period, and hover over the lines for values.
  • Each bucket tab also has a by-product table (with each commodity's Equal Weight portfolio) and a cumulative-return chart for any single commodity.

Methodology and data

Timing convention (all five sleeves)

  • 1-day lag: every signal is generated from closing prices on day t. The position is taken at the close of day t+1 and earns the return from that close onward, so a signal never trades on the price it was computed from. Formally, the position held over day t is wt = st−2, where s is the sleeve's signal, and it earns that day's log return, ln(Pt/Pt−1). Transaction costs of 5 bps per unit of turnover are charged when the position changes, and on every roll day.

Sleeves (per product)

  • Momentum: average of the signs of three moving-average crossovers, (1,20), (5,60), (20,250), on the raw front-month price.
    $$s_t=\tfrac13\sum_{(a,b)}\operatorname{sign}\!\big(\mathrm{MA}_a(P)_t-\mathrm{MA}_b(P)_t\big),\quad (a,b)\in\{(1,20),(5,60),(20,250)\}$$
  • Carry (V2): For each tenor pair, the carry slope (near - far) / near is standardised against its own trailing 252-day mean and standard deviation. The z-scores of a product's tenor pairs are summed (two pairs for every product) and the sign of the sum is the signal. The position is flat only when the sum is exactly zero. If a z-score is missing, the previous signal is carried forward.
    $$c^{(k)}_t=\frac{P^{\mathrm{near},k}_t-P^{\mathrm{far},k}_t}{P^{\mathrm{near},k}_t},\qquad z^{(k)}_t=\frac{c^{(k)}_t-\mu^{252}_t\!\big(c^{(k)}\big)}{\sigma^{252}_t\!\big(c^{(k)}\big)}$$$$s_t=\operatorname{sign}\!\Big(\sum_k z^{(k)}_t\Big)$$
  • Carry-Momentum (V3): change of the carry slope over 20 observations, summed across the tenor pairs (raw changes, not standardised) and signed; if a pair is missing the last signal is kept.
    $$s_t=\operatorname{sign}\!\Big(\sum_k\big(c^{(k)}_t-c^{(k)}_{t-20}\big)\Big)$$
  • Value: price of the Value contract (F3; F2 for Precious and Agriculture, whose contract cycles are sparse, so F3 can sit 4 to 6 months from the front) against its own 1,260-day average, long below -10%, short above +10%.
    $$d_t=\frac{P^{V}_t}{\frac1{1260}\sum_{i=0}^{1259}P^{V}_{t-i}}-1,\qquad s_t=+1\;\text{if }d_t<-10\%,\;\;-1\;\text{if }d_t>+10\%,\;\;0\;\text{otherwise}$$
  • Skewness: minus the skewness of the product's daily log returns (roll-adjusted series) over the past 252 observations; long when negative, short when positive (after Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes and Miffre 2021, time-series version).
    $$\hat\gamma_t=\frac{\frac1{252}\sum_{i=0}^{251}(r_{t-i}-\bar r)^3}{\Big(\frac1{252}\sum_{i=0}^{251}(r_{t-i}-\bar r)^2\Big)^{3/2}},\qquad s_t=-\operatorname{sign}(\hat\gamma_t)$$

Tenor pairs (Carry and Carry-Momentum)

  • Metals, Petroleum and Nat Gas: F1-F3 and F1-F13. NGL: F2-F4 and F2-F14, except Naphtha F2-F4 only. TTF and UK Gas: F1-F2 and F1-F13. EUA: F1-F2 and F1-F5 (EUA is quarterly, so F5 is 12 months out; TTF is monthly, so F13 is).
  • Precious: F1-F2 plus a long pair about 12 months out: Gold F1-F7, Silver F1-F6, Platinum F1-F5, Palladium F1-F5.
  • Agriculture: F1-F2 plus a long pair about 12 months out: Corn F1-F6, Wheat F1-F6, Soybean F1-F8, Soybean Oil F1-F8, Coffee F1-F6, Sugar F1-F5.

Rolling

  • Each contract is rolled on the 5th trading day of the month in which its last trade date falls. The series is bridged on the day after the last trade date, when the data's F1 switches contract. Counted from the roll day to the last trade date, this rolls about 5 trading days before expiry for Corn, Wheat, Soybean and Soybean Oil, 6 for Metals, 8 for Coffee, 9 for WTI, 11 for Brent and EUA, 14 for Nat Gas and Precious, 15 for TTF, UK Gas and Sugar, and 16 for RBOB, Heating Oil, NGL and Naphtha.

How things are combined

  • Buckets: Petroleum = WTI, Brent, RBOB, Heating Oil. Gas and Emissions = Henry Hub natural gas (US), TTF natural gas (European, ICE Endex), UK Gas (NBP, ICE Futures Europe) and EUA carbon. NGL = Ethane, Propane, Butane, Isobutane and Naphtha (CIF NWE average-price swap). Metals, Precious and Agriculture are unchanged.
  • Products inside a sleeve are equally weighted on common dates (a dropped date's move is carried into the next shared date).
  • Each bucket portfolio combines its five sleeves by EW PORT (equal weight) or Inverse Vol (weights from each sleeve's trailing 63-day volatility, recomputed daily).
  • Combined books are two-stage: sleeves into a bucket portfolio, then the six bucket portfolios into one book; all four EW / Inverse Vol pairs are shown. Cross-pair portfolios blend two buckets' portfolios the same way. Series are aligned on common dates before weighting.

Liquidity metric

  • Dollar risk turnover: the amount of one-standard-deviation daily price risk a market trades per day, which puts contracts of different size, price and volatility on one scale.
    $$c_i=m_i\,\bar P_i\,\sigma_i,\qquad \mathrm{ADV}_i=\frac1{T_i}\sum_{t=1}^{T_i}\sum_{j\in S_i}V_{i,j,t},\qquad x_i=\mathrm{ADV}_i\,c_i,\qquad L_i=\frac{K}{x_i}$$
  • Terms: mi contract multiplier (units per lot); P̄i mean price of the contract held over the window (USD per unit); σi standard deviation of the daily log returns of the roll-adjusted series over the window; Si the strip of tenors spanning twelve months (F1-F12 for monthly chains; Gold F1-F6, Silver F1-F5, Platinum and Palladium F1-F4, Corn, Wheat and Coffee F1-F5, Soybean F1-F7, Soybean Oil F1-F8, Sugar F1-F4, EUA F1-F4); Vi,j,t volume in lots of tenor j on day t (a day without a print counts as zero, open interest is never used); Ti the trading days of the window on the product's own calendar.
  • L (days): K is a reference position of USD 1 million of one-sigma daily risk, and L is its size as a multiple of one day of the market's risk turnover, i.e. the time in days to trade it at full market participation (0.05 is five per cent of a day, 3 is three days of the entire market's flow). It is shown as Time to trade 1 sigma risk (in Days) in each By-product table. The ranking of products does not depend on K.
  • For research purposes the metric has been evaluated on 2025 volumes for each product (a one-time snapshot); NGL volume is the CME half only.

Data and calendars

  • Prices run through 2026-10-29 for all six buckets (LME and NGL through 2026-10-28): the 29-Oct Bloomberg pull merged into the 24-Sep history, nothing cut. Reporting starts 2012-01-01; the 2026 year-to-date column covers 1 January to 29 October. Value requires two years of price history of its contract (F3; F2 for Precious and Agriculture) before its first signal.
  • Roll calendars: Expiry dates for Precious and Agriculture are taken from Bloomberg and follow its contract-month chain. Metals, Energy (including Henry Hub) and the Mont Belvieu NGL swaps use expiry dates published by the exchange.

Regimes

  • Reporting periods: P1 covers 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2016, P2 covers 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2021, and P3 covers 1 January 2022 to 29 October 2026 (the last price date; LME and NGL end on 28 October). The periods are consecutive and do not overlap. The 2026 year-to-date column falls within P3. Each period's statistics are computed on that period alone: return and volatility are annualised over the period, and maximum drawdown is measured from the period's start.
